learning_objectives.objective: Calculate the mean, median, and mode for a given real-world data set.
Compare different measures of center to determine which best represents the central tendency of a data set based on data distribution characteristics.
Interpret measures of center in the context of a real-world problem by explaining what the values represent in terms of the original data situation.
Interpret measures of variability in the context of a real-world problem by explaining what the range and interquartile range reveal about data spread.
Describe the center and spread of data displayed in dot plots, histograms, or box plots using appropriate statistical terminology.
Identify the shape of data distributions as approximately symmetric or skewed when analyzing graphical displays.
Identify unusual features in data graphs including gaps, peaks, clusters, and extreme values.
Describe the real-world context that produced a given data set by analyzing patterns and characteristics visible in its graphical representation.
Write examples of statistical questions that anticipate variability in responses.
Write non-examples of statistical questions by creating questions that have single, deterministic answers.
Explain why a given question is statistical by identifying how it anticipates variability in the data collected.
Compare rational numbers using inequality symbols when presented with or without a number line.
Order sets of rational numbers from least to greatest or greatest to least.
Compare absolute values of rational numbers to determine which has greater distance from zero.
Solve real-world problems by applying comparison and ordering of rational numbers.
Explain the meaning of absolute value as the distance from zero on a number line.
Calculate the absolute value of positive and negative rational numbers.
Apply absolute value concepts to solve real-world problems involving distance, temperature, or other contexts where magnitude matters.
Identify ordered pairs that are reflections of each other across the y-axis by comparing their x-coordinates and y-coordinates.
Identify ordered pairs that are reflections of each other across the x-axis by comparing their x-coordinates and y-coordinates.
Identify the quadrant location of an ordered pair by analyzing the signs of its x-coordinate and y-coordinate.
Graph ordered pairs accurately in all four quadrants of the coordinate plane.
Calculate distances between two points that share the same x-coordinate or y-coordinate.
Solve real-world problems by interpreting coordinates and calculating distances on the coordinate plane.
Identify opposite numbers as pairs of numbers located on opposite sides of zero on a number line.
Explain that opposite numbers are always the same distance from zero on a number line using examples of integer pairs.
Apply rational numbers to represent quantities in real-world contexts such as temperature, elevation, or account balances.
Explain what zero represents in different real-world situations involving rational numbers.
Use positive and negative numbers to describe quantities with opposite directions such as above and below sea level or gains and losses.
Represent real-world quantities using appropriate positive and negative rational numbers.
Add multi-digit decimals using a standard algorithm.
Subtract multi-digit decimals using a standard algorithm.
Multiply multi-digit decimals using a standard algorithm.
Divide multi-digit decimals using a standard algorithm.
Determine the prime factorization of whole numbers using factors and multiples.
Divide multi-digit whole numbers fluently using a standard algorithm.
Solve real-world problems that require division of multi-digit whole numbers.
Identify the greatest common factor in sums of two whole numbers by finding shared factors between the addends.
Apply the distributive property to factor out the greatest common factor from sums of whole numbers using correct mathematical notation.
Express factored sums as a product of the common factor and a sum of two whole numbers that have no common factors.
Analyze word problems to determine when division of fractions is required for the solution.
Solve problems involving quotients of fractions by applying division algorithms and interpreting results in context.
Express proportional relationships using fraction notation, colon notation, and word form.
Describe relationships between quantities using appropriate ratio language.
Solve percent problems using ratio and rate reasoning with tables, tape diagrams, or double number lines.
Solve measurement conversion problems by applying ratio and rate reasoning.
Solve problems involving equivalent ratios using tables of equivalent ratios, tape diagrams, double number lines, or equations.
Calculate unit rates from given ratio relationships.
Describe ratio relationships by expressing them as unit rates with appropriate units.
Determine whether two algebraic expressions are equivalent by applying properties of operations.
Justify whether two algebraic expressions are equivalent by explaining the mathematical reasoning used in the comparison.
Generate equivalent algebraic expressions by applying the commutative property of addition and multiplication.
Generate equivalent algebraic expressions by applying the associative property of addition and multiplication.
Generate equivalent algebraic expressions by applying the distributive property.
Generate equivalent algebraic expressions by applying inverse properties of addition and multiplication.
Generate equivalent algebraic expressions by applying identity properties of addition and multiplication.
Write expressions involving whole number exponents to represent mathematical situations.
Evaluate expressions involving whole number exponents using order of operations.
Compare expressions involving whole number exponents by determining their relative values.
Evaluate expressions containing absolute value using the correct order of operations.
Evaluate expressions containing whole number exponents using the correct order of operations.
Evaluate expressions containing both absolute value and whole number exponents using the correct order of operations.
Identify terms in an algebraic expression using correct mathematical vocabulary.
Identify coefficients in an algebraic expression using correct mathematical vocabulary.
Identify factors in an algebraic expression using correct mathematical vocabulary.
Identify sums, products, and quotients in an algebraic expression using correct mathematical vocabulary.
Interpret variables as unknown values within the context of given mathematical problems.
Explain what values a variable can represent based on the constraints of a specific problem context.
Write algebraic expressions to represent verbal mathematical statements.
Write algebraic expressions to represent quantitative relationships in real-world scenarios.
Create tables to represent the relationship between independent and dependent variables.
Create graphs to represent the relationship between independent and dependent variables.
Write equations to represent the relationship between independent and dependent variables.
Determine whether a given value is a solution to an equation by using substitution.
Determine whether a given value is a solution to an inequality by using substitution.
Interpret the solution of an equation by explaining what it means within the context of the original problem situation.
Interpret the solution of an inequality by explaining what it means within the context of the original problem situation.
Represent solutions of inequalities on a number line using appropriate symbols and notation.
Explain why the solution set of an inequality may contain infinitely many solutions.
Calculate the perimeter of a polygon graphed in the coordinate plane using coordinate geometry.
Calculate the area of a polygon graphed in the coordinate plane using coordinate geometry.
Determine missing vertices of a rectangle in the coordinate plane when vertices share the same x-coordinate.
Determine missing vertices of a rectangle in the coordinate plane when vertices share the same y-coordinate.
Calculate the length of a horizontal side using coordinates of points that have the same y-coordinate.
Calculate the length of a vertical side using coordinates of points that have the same x-coordinate.
Calculate the volume of right rectangular prisms using the formula V = lwh.
Calculate the volume of right rectangular prisms using the formula V = Bh.
Compare volumes of different right rectangular prisms by calculating and analyzing their respective volumes.
Decompose irregular polygons into triangles and rectangles to find total area.
Compose smaller polygons to form larger shapes and calculate the combined area.
Apply composing and decomposing techniques to solve real-world area problems.
Create nets composed of rectangles and triangles to represent three-dimensional figures.
Calculate the surface area of three-dimensional figures using their corresponding nets.
Apply surface area calculations to solve real-world mathematical problems.
